messages:
sara: Hey team — urgent customer report: frontend app deployed to Vercel Edge is getting 401s when calling the Redwood edge SDK from the browser. Works when called from our server. Repro attached.
kevin_support: Which SDK/version and exact environment (browser, bundler, runtime)?
sara: SDK: @redwood/inference-edge@0.13.2 (bundled in SPA via Vite). Env: Vite 4 dev build and production on Vercel Edge Functions. Browser: Chrome 112 / Mac. Steps:
1) Build SPA with edge bundle
2) From client run SDK call
3) Observe preflight then 401 on actual request
sara: Repro code (simplified):
```ts
// client code in browser
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-edge'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: PUBLIC_RW_TOKEN })
await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'rw-small', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }] })
```
sara: Network trace shows OPTIONS preflight returns 200, then POST returns 401. Response headers from API (actual):
```http
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
access-control-allow-origin: https://app.customer.com
access-control-allow-credentials: false
# no Access-Control-Allow-Headers present
```
michael_dev: :thinking: If the server doesn't include Access-Control-Allow-Headers that lists Authorization, the browser blocks the actual request. But you said preflight returned 200 — can you paste the OPTIONS response headers exactly (including Access-Control-Allow-Headers)?
sara: Confirmed: OPTIONS had Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, GET; Access-Control-Allow-Origin present; but Access-Control-Allow-Headers missing. So browser does the actual request but API returns 401 (looks like token not being accepted, maybe the header was stripped or server requires additional header). Full OPTIONS/POST headers attached above.
kevin_support: Two possibilities:
- API is not returning the required Access-Control-Allow-Headers (Authorization, Content-Type) for the route. That will cause flaky behavior.
- Or the SDK bundling/polyfill in the browser is doing something odd to headers. Which bundler polyfills are enabled in Vite? Are you shipping any node-fetch/polyfill that could change behavior?
olivia: We've seen similar: our edge SDK used a node-oriented fetch polyfill in older releases which sometimes interacted poorly with edge runtimes / bundlers and caused headers to be normalized or dropped. Can you try a quick repro with the browser calling a plain fetch (no SDK) to the same endpoint with Authorization header to see if it's an SDK-specific issue?
sara: Tried plain fetch (same token): browser POST -> 401, exact same behavior. OPTIONS still lacked Access-Control-Allow-Headers. So server is the root cause here. Customer likely hit a CORS config gap on the API gateway in front of the hosted endpoint.
kevin_support: Good triage. Short-term workarounds:
- Add Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type to the API response (preferred fix).
- Proxy requests through your own server (server-side endpoint) so the browser never sends the secret to the API directly.
- If you must call from browser, use a short-lived public key/token designed for browser usage (rotate frequently) or the hosted client token flow.
michael_dev: For SDK improvements: we will add clearer docs and a runtime check that emits a warning when people bundle the edge/server SDK into public browser bundles. Also a fix landed in master to avoid polyfill fetch shims by default — upgrade to @redwood/inference-edge@0.13.4 when released. That should reduce bundling footguns but it won't change server CORS headers.
olivia: Vercel note: Edge Functions run at the edge and shouldn't mutate Authorization, but if you added any middleware or rewrites (Vercel middleware) make sure they preserve headers. Also double-check any CDN or API gateway (we've seen customers with Cloudflare rules stripping Authorization on OPTIONS).
kevin_support: Action items for support:
- sara: open a support ticket with customer's domain, the failing request/response headers (OPTIONS & POST) and the token id.
- engineering: add a short doc blurb warning about bundling server SDK into browser apps, and add a CORS troubleshooting checklist.
sara: Will open ticket now and include the headers + repro snippet. Customer will use server-side proxy as immediate workaround. Thanks all :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: NOTE: created ticket #SUP-1248 for customer "Acme Co" — assigned to kevin_support.
michael_dev: I'll post a small PR to add the fetch fallback opt-out docs and a note in the readme about browser usage.
sara: Perfect — marking this thread resolved for now, will update if customer still sees failures after proxying. :eyes:
